hero.title: San Bernardino
hero.subtitle: Lakeside living, mature landscape and genuine privacy, under an hour from Asunción.

intro.title: A place to live differently
intro.text: San Bernardino sits on the eastern shore of Lake Ypacaraí, forty-eight kilometres from Asunción. It combines still water, mature trees and a strongly residential character with an identity of its own — the town was founded by German settlers in the 1880s and still shows it. Close enough to the capital to matter, far enough for the pace to change.

experiences.title: Ordinary days, raised by the setting

items.title: Sunsets over the water
items.description: Lake Ypacaraí turns the end of the day into the moment that defines San Bernardino. Light, water and open horizon produce an atmosphere that is calm and unmistakably residential.

items.title: Clubs, sailing and social life
items.description: A long tradition of yacht clubs and water sport gives the town a social and sporting dimension valued by families, second-home owners and anyone who wants an active life on the water.

items.title: Food with its own character
items.description: Restaurants, cafés and historic patisseries are part of the experience here. San Bernardino combines German heritage, Paraguayan cooking and contemporary kitchens at a relaxed, walkable scale.

distances.title: Everything close, when you need it

living.title: What to know before living in San Bernardino

items.title: Beaches and the lake
items.text: Lake Ypacaraí dominates the landscape. Its shoreline holds walks, clubs, town beaches and open-air space in use all year.

items.title: Shopping and services
items.text: Supermarkets, pharmacies, medical centres and convenience shops in town, with fast connections to the larger retail centres of San Lorenzo and Asunción.

items.title: Festivals and social life
items.text: Through the summer the town fills with concerts, cultural events, markets and festivals at venues such as the José Asunción Flores amphitheatre and Casa Hassler.

items.title: Where to eat
items.text: The range runs from traditional restaurants and cafés to German heritage patisseries and contemporary kitchens that follow the rhythm of the season.

gastronomy.title: A food scene with its own character

items.name: Bistró Del Val
items.description: Carefully judged cooking in an intimate room. Suited to quiet dinners.

items.name: Café Francés
items.description: A local institution of European inspiration, valued for its kitchen and unhurried atmosphere.

items.name: La Alemana
items.description: A San Bernardino landmark, known for its baking and its link to the town's German heritage.

market.title: A market with depth and direction
market.text: San Bernardino has neither over-developed nor lost its character — rare for a lakeside town within an hour of a capital city. Shoreline land is finite and there is no meaningful new development, while demand from families choosing to live here year-round rather than seasonally continues to grow. Paraguay places no restriction on foreign ownership of urban property: full freehold title, no residency requirement.
highlights: Finite lakeside land, no new development
Full freehold ownership for foreign buyers
One hour from the capital and its airport
